errors.unknownProtocol: Unknown protocol “__protocol__” (possible: Modbus TCP, web server, MQTT)
errors.noAddress: “__name__”: no address known (neither operand nor Modbus address)
errors.otherNet: “__name__” belongs to NET station __net__ – read it via this protocol on the device with NET ID __net__
errors.noModbus: “__name__” (send/receive bit) cannot be reached via Modbus

test.okMw: Connection OK – MW1 = __value__ (clock data not enabled in easySoft)
test.okNoData: Connection OK – the easyE4 answers, but neither clock data nor MW1 are enabled (easySoft: Modbus server tab)
test.switched: – with addressing “__mode__”. Please apply this setting.

exception.1: Function not supported by the easyE4
exception.2: Address does not exist or is not enabled in easySoft (Modbus server tab)
exception.2w: Cannot write: address not enabled, “read only” or “set clock locked” (easySoft: Modbus server tab)

errors.queueFull: Too many pending requests – increase the polling interval
errors.indexRangeFw: __what__: with the selected firmware only up to __max__ (more from firmware 2.40)
errors.rangeOrder: Range: the end must be greater than or equal to the start
errors.badOperand: “__text__” is not a valid operand (examples: MW3, Q1, IA2, M1-M16, CLOCK)
errors.badBool: “__value__” is not a bit value (true/false, 1/0, on/off)
errors.badNumber: __what__: “__value__” must be a whole number from __min__ to __max__
errors.notWritable: __type__ cannot be written via Modbus (only M, MB, MW, MD, N, NB, NW, ND)
errors.badFc: Function code __fc__ is not possible here
errors.badAddr: Register no. must be between 1 and 65536

apiError.8: Invalid number (index) – does the operand exist in the device?
apiError.32: This function block does not exist
apiError.33: This block number does not exist in the program
apiError.34: Connection type does not fit this block
apiError.35: Connection number does not fit this block
apiError.36: Word input is not connected to a constant in the program
apiError.unknown: API error __code__ (see Eaton documentation “API Error Codes”)

http.400: Request rejected (400): command unknown or misspelled
http.401: Login rejected (401): check user/password or API key
http.403: Not allowed (403): check permissions in easySoft; date/time only in STOP
http.404: Not found (404): is the easyE4 web server switched on?
http.501: Not supported (501): this firmware does not have this function
http.401set: No permission (401): this user is not allowed to do this – check permissions in easySoft (write markers, operating mode “mode”, clock “clock”)
http.401adm: No permission (401): only the user “admin” may change the device name and admin settings

errors.tls: HTTPS connection to __host__ failed (__msg__): encryption or certificate not accepted. Switch off “Verify certificate” or try http.
errors.queueFull: Too many simultaneous requests (increase the polling interval)
errors.noValue: no answer for this value (does the operand exist in the device?)
errors.badMode: Operating mode must be RUN or STOP
errors.netRange: NET ID must be between 0 and 8
errors.rangeOrder: Range: the end must be greater than or equal to the start
errors.invalidValue: Invalid value: number or true/false expected
errors.notWritable: __type__ cannot be written via the web server (only M, MB, MW, MD, N, NB, NW, ND)

test.ok: Connection OK – the easyE4 sends __n__ values (e.g. __sample__)
test.offline: Broker reachable, but the easyE4 reports “not connected” (connected = false)
test.noData: Broker reachable, but no data from the easyE4 within __s__ s. Check: base topic correct? easyE4 in RUN? Operands entered in easySoft under “Cyclic data”?

errors.noBaseTopic: Base topic missing (e.g. “easye4/1” if easySoft shows easye4/1/data etc.) – or enter all four topics separately
errors.badTopic: Topic “__topic__” is invalid (no + or #, at most 511 characters)
errors.auth: Login at the MQTT broker rejected: check user/password
errors.deviceOffline: The easyE4 is not connected to the broker (connected = false)
errors.noData: no value yet – easyE4 in RUN? Is the operand listed in easySoft under “Cyclic data”?
errors.outputNotWritable: “__name__”: outputs cannot be written via MQTT
errors.reserved: “__name__” cannot be written via MQTT (I1–I16, IA1–IA4, ID1–ID25 are reserved)
errors.badNumber: “__name__”: “__value__” must be a whole number from __min__ to __max__
errors.actionTimeout: No answer from the easyE4 to “__op__” within __s__ s
errors.badMode: Operating mode must be RUN or STOP
errors.cert: TLS connection to __host__ rejected (__msg__): the broker certificate does not match the given CA file (ca.crt) or has expired
errors.certName: TLS connection to __host__ rejected (__msg__): the address “__name__” is not in the broker certificate – connect using the name or IP the certificate was issued for

errors.noName: Please enter a name for the device
errors.notRunning: Device __id__ is currently not being polled (switched off?)
errors.secretsLocked: The stored passwords are encrypted and cannot be read here
errors.badScale: Conversion incomplete: enter both points (raw value and value) as numbers; the two raw values must differ.
errors.notConnected: Not connected – click “Connect” at the top right

warn.notInItf: __op__ (__name__) is in the program but not in the .itf – readable via Modbus only once it is enabled in easySoft (Modbus server tab)
warn.nameTwice: Name “__name__” belongs to __a__ and __b__ – __b__ is therefore called “__new__”
warn.foreign: __op____name__ belongs to NET station __net__ – read it on the device with NET ID __net__
warn.snrn: __op____name__: send/receive bit – not reachable via Modbus, for information only
warn.removed: __name__ (__op__) is no longer contained in the import
warn.fwMismatch: Attention: the .itf file matches firmware “__itf__”, the device is set to “__dev__”. Does the file come from another device? Then many variables will get no values. Choose the right .itf or change the firmware of the device.
warn.noSt: No ST program included: normal for FBD/LD. Names then come from the symbol table or the operand comments (.xls).
warn.noItf: No .itf file chosen: easy4Visu calculates the Modbus addresses itself from operand and firmware (checked on the device). Areas that are not enabled only show up when reading.

manual.badOperand: “__text__” is not an easyE4 operand (examples: MW3, I01, Q02, M5, MD20, IA1, 2NW3)

devices.title: Devices
devices.intro: Add your easyE4 devices here. Then read in the variables from your easySoft project under “Variables”.
devices.emptyHint: Add your first easyE4 – all you need is its IP address and the protocol.

editDevice.name: Name

protocols.modbusHint: Fast and simple. In easySoft, switch on the Modbus TCP server and enable the areas.
protocols.jsonHint: Via the built-in web server of the easyE4, with user and password or API key.
protocols.mqttHint: The easyE4 itself sends via an MQTT broker (firmware 2.40 or newer).

editDevice.netIdHint: only needed in a NET network (1 … 8)
editDevice.secretKeep: saved – leave empty to keep it
editDevice.baseTopicHint: as in easySoft, e.g. easye4/1 (then easye4/1/data etc.)
editDevice.ownTopics: Own topics instead of base topic
editDevice.deleteConfirm: Really delete “__name__”? The variables read in will be lost.

detail.importHint: Choose the files from easySoft: the variable list (.itf), for FBD/LD the operand comments (.xls), for ST the symbol table (.csv) and/or the ST program (copied from easySoft and saved as a .txt text file).
detail.empty: No variables yet. Read them in from your easySoft project.
detail.selectHint: Tick on the left to delete
detail.noDevice: No device yet. First add your easyE4 under “Devices”.
detail.rowHint: Click to edit (display name, suggestion, unit, delete)

importDlg.title: Read in variables
importDlg.applied: __added__ new, __removed__ removed – your own changes have been kept

varDlg.operandHint: as in easySoft, e.g. MW3, I01, Q02, M5, MD20, IA1 – for NET partners 2NW3
varDlg.name: Name (as in easySoft)
varDlg.label: Display name
varDlg.labelHint: shown like this on the operating page; empty = automatic
varDlg.scaleHint: The easyE4 often delivers a raw value (e.g. 0 … 1000 for 0 … 10 V). Enter two points and the visualisation shows the value in the unit everywhere – including trends – and converts setpoints back when writing. Empty = raw value as before.

page.title: Operating pages
page.intro: One page per device, created automatically from the suggestions. You can rebuild them later in the editor.
page.empty: No operating page yet – first add a device and read in its variables.
page.noElements: Nothing to show for this device yet. Set “Display” or “Operation” for the variables.
page.unconfirmed: sent – the easyE4 still reports __value__ (does the program reset the value?)
page.unassignedHint: __n__ variables have no suggestion yet and are only displayed. Under “Variables” → “Edit” → “Use”, set them to “Operation” to get switches and setpoints.
page.introEditor: Here you operate your plant with the pages you create in the editor.
page.noPagesHint: In the editor you put your pages together: drag variables onto the page, done. Here you operate them afterwards.
page.noPagesGuest: Log in as technician to set up.
page.emptyPage: This page is still empty. In the editor you drag elements and variables onto it.
page.notConnected: Not connected – click “Connect” at the top right to operate.
page.clockDrift: The easyE4 clock differs from the PC clock by __n__ min.

assign.title: What should go on the operating page?
assign.intro: Inputs and outputs are always displayed. For the markers you decide here whether they are displayed or operated. A clear name helps on the operating page.
assign.changingHint: Markers marked “changing” are currently changing their value by themselves – they are usually written by the controller, so they are rather a display.
assign.none: No markers to assign – inputs and outputs are displayed automatically.

options.title: Settings
options.autoPagesHint: Creates a ready page with displays, switches and setpoints from the variables of a device – without the editor. Appears on the left under “Operating pages”.
options.quickAssignHint: After reading in, decide which markers are displayed or operated (for the automatic operating page).
options.commissioningHint: Shows “sending”, “applied” and controller errors in plain text for every element on the operating pages. Switch off for normal operation.
options.designHint: Colours, corners, font and logo for the operating pages – with preview and readability check.
options.licHint: easy4Visu is open source (MIT licence) and uses components by other authors. All licence texts are shown here.
options.licIntro: easy4Visu __v__. The texts are also in the installation folder (LICENSE.easy4visu.txt, LIZENZEN-DRITTER.txt).
options.autostartHint: Starts easy4Visu when you log on to Windows and restarts it within one minute after a crash or after the window was closed. To close it for good: “Close easy4Visu”.
options.connectOnStartHint: Connects to all devices right at start.
options.startOperateHint: Shows the start page in full screen right after start. Leaving only as technician once there are users.
options.quitHint: Closes easy4Visu for good (technicians only). Closing the window, Alt+F4 or the Task Manager count as a failure instead: with “Start with Windows”, easy4Visu comes back within at most 1 minute.
options.kioskAll: For operation at the machine, also switch on “Connect at start” and “Start in operating mode”?

editor.libHint: Drag onto the page or click
editor.libHelp: Drag onto the page – the element lands exactly there. A click puts it on an empty spot (into a frame only if that frame is selected).
editor.varHint: Drag onto the page or onto an element, double-click inserts
editor.varHelp: Drag a variable onto the page – the matching element is created by itself. Dragged onto an existing element, it replaces its variable. ✓ = already on this page.
editor.noDevices: No device yet. Add it under “Devices” and read in its variables.
editor.dropFirst: Drag an element or a variable here
editor.deletePageConfirm: Delete page “__name__” with everything on it?
editor.lastPage: The last page cannot be deleted.
editor.pageHelp: Click an element to edit it. Ctrl+click or drawing a box = several. Arrow keys move, Del deletes, Ctrl+D copies, Ctrl+Z undoes.
editor.varChoose: Choose the variable the element should show or operate.
editor.varMissing: This variable no longer exists (device deleted or read in again). Please choose again.
editor.label: Label
editor.frameAroundHint: Puts a frame around the selection. Whatever lies completely inside then belongs to the frame.
editor.frameAroundNo: No room for a frame: it would partly cover another element. Make some space first.
editor.frameTitleNoRoom: The heading covers the content – make the frame a little larger or make room above it.
editor.elHelp: Drag the element = move, bottom right corner = size. Red lines show when it is flush with another one.
editor.textHint: Values appear at the placeholders {1}, {2} … – “Insert variable” below.
editor.placeholdersHint: The variable is inserted at the cursor as {1}, {2} … Unit empty = without unit.
editor.symbolHint: Without a symbol a status message shows a light dot. A symbol in the states takes priority.

map.title: Value list
map.hint: Per value or range: text, colour, symbol. The first matching row applies; “otherwise” for all other values.
map.numberHint: E.g. warning from 80, fault from 95. A text replaces the number.
map.gaugeHint: Ranges “from … to” with a colour appear on the scale, e.g. 0 … 60 on, 60 … 80 warning, 80 … 100 fault. The needle takes the colour of its range.

modeHint.pulse: Pulse: sends a 1 when pressed, the easyE4 program resets the marker itself.
modeHint.toggle: Latching: first press = 1, second press = 0. Without feedback the button lights up while its variable is 1.

editor.fbColorHint: The button lights up in this colour while the feedback is 1 (latching button without feedback: its own variable).
editor.scaleTicksHint: Major ticks with numbers in round steps, minor ticks in between.
editor.gaugeTicksHint: The numbers are on the same side as the ticks.
editor.resizeWH: Drag to change width and height
editor.pageWidthHint: Best choose the size of the operating screen. Editor and operating page show the page exactly the same – on other screens scaled up or down to fit.
editor.tabletHint: Tablets report fewer pixels than their display has – the list already contains these values.
editor.pageScrollHint: Off (default): the page always fits the screen completely. On: elements below the screen can be reached by scrolling.
editor.pageStartHint: The operating pages start with this page.
editor.phoneHint: For phone pages in the browser: the page fills the width of the phone and scrolls down. Large switches and few elements stacked vertically are easiest to operate.
editor.pageWebHint: Off: the page exists only on the PC; in the browser it is missing along with its page key.
editor.offscreen: Below the screen – not visible in operation. Drag it further up, make it smaller or switch on “Page may scroll” for the page.
editor.offscreenCount: __n__ element(s) lie below the screen and are not visible in operation.

image.type: Please choose an image: PNG, JPG, GIF, WebP or SVG.
image.size: The image is too large – please choose an image up to 10 MB.
image.fitHint: Fit shows the whole image, Fill crops the edges, Original size shows it in real size (centred).
image.altHint: Short text, e.g. “Company logo” – for screen readers and if the image is missing.
image.help: The image fills its space – set the size at the bottom right corner.
image.swapHint: The list below belongs to this variable; each row can also check another variable.

bg.title: Page background
bg.hint: Elements in a frame stay easy to read. Elements without a frame sit directly on the background – make sure there is enough contrast there.

editor.rasterHint: Show/hide the dot grid (elements snap every 10 pixels)
editor.sameSizeHint: The first selected element sets the size.
editor.kpiAddrHint: Small below the value: variable name, operand and device (e.g. “Fuellstand · MW51 · NT1”).
editor.choiceHint: A click writes the value into the variable (e.g. 0 = Off, 1 = Manual, 2 = Automatic). The button whose value the controller reports is highlighted.
editor.heartbeatHint: Optional: a marker word that the controller program keeps counting up. If the number stops, the program is not running.
editor.trendSeriesHint: Up to 4 curves, each with its own scale (bottom / top). You can also drag a variable onto the trend. Curves are only shown if the variable is recorded.
editor.trendFull: A trend has at most 4 curves.
editor.deleteItemsConfirm: Delete __n__ elements (a frame takes its content with it)?
editor.elsHelp: Ctrl+click selects more elements, drawing a box on a free area selects all inside. Dragging a selected element moves all. Arrow keys = 10 pixels, with Alt 1.
editor.geometryHint: Dragging works too: move the element, bottom right corner = size. Hold Alt for single pixels.
editor.frameHelp: A frame groups elements: whatever lies completely inside moves with it and is copied with it (Ctrl+D = e.g. “Pump 2”).
editor.fbHint: The button lights up while this variable is 1 (e.g. Q1 “pump running”) – so you can see that the controller has taken over the command.
editor.overlapBack: There is already an element there – moved back.
editor.overlapNo: There is already an element there.

state.title: Display per status
state.hint: The topmost matching row wins – so put faults at the top. Each row checks a value (or range "to") or a bit (on/off). If no row matches, "otherwise" applies.
state.hintImage: The topmost matching row wins – so put faults at the top. Each row checks a value (or range "to") or a bit (on/off). If no row matches or it has no image, the image above is shown.
state.otherVarHint: This row checks another variable, e.g. a fault

editor.labelFromVar: Empty = name from the variable list. That name is translated under "Languages".
editor.clockFmtHint: Shows the easyE4 clock – even if only one part of the clock (e.g. the minute from the .itf list) is selected.
editor.clockWarn: Warn if the clock is wrong
editor.clockWarnHint: Shows ⚠ if the easyE4 clock differs from the PC clock by 1 minute or more (e.g. after a daylight saving change). The PC must have the right time.
editor.clockIncomplete: Only one part of the clock (e.g. the minute) is in the variable list. Add the whole clock for hour, minute and date – easy4Visu then reads it in one piece.
editor.clockMqtt: Over MQTT the clock only arrives if it is listed in easySoft under “Cyclic data” (all parts of the clock).
editor.visHint: Only shown and operable on the operating page while the condition is met (no value, e.g. not connected: hidden). A frame takes its contents along. In the editor half transparent with 👁.
editor.visBadge: Only visible while the condition is met

online.connectHint: Connect to all enabled devices now – afterwards operating pages write to the real controller
online.disconnectHint: Close the connection to all devices
online.connected: Connected – operating pages now act on the controller

mqtt.part: Only some MQTT brokers are reachable

design.logoType: The logo must be an image: PNG, JPG or SVG.
design.logoSize: The logo is too large – please choose an image up to 1 MB.
design.importBad: This file is not an easy4Visu colour theme.
design.title: Design of the operating pages
design.intro: Applies to the operating pages and to the page in the editor. Changes are saved immediately.
design.resetConfirm: Reset colours, corners, font and logo to the default?
design.deriveHint: E.g. choose your company colour – readable colours for light and dark are derived from it. The state colours (on, warning, fault) stay.
design.colorsHint: Per meaning for light and dark. Next to each colour you see whether it stands out well on the background. Text on buttons adapts by itself.

rolesHint.control: Buttons, switch buttons, operating mode, function keys, plus/minus

design.depthHint: Subtle: buttons, mode selectors and function keys stand out slightly and sink in when pressed; frames cast a soft shadow.
design.fontHint: Atkinson Hyperlegible is especially easy to read.
design.sizeHint: “large” for operator panels read from a distance.
design.logoHint: PNG, JPG or SVG up to 1 MB. Appears at the top of the operating pages.
design.presetNoName: Please enter a name for the template.
design.presetSaveHint: Saves the current design (colours, corners, font, size, logo). Same name = replace.
design.presetDeleteConfirm: Delete template “__name__”? The current design stays.

bars.title: Bars (template for all pages)
bars.intro: You design the bars once – they appear on all operating pages. On a single page you can hide them (page settings).
bars.help: Add blocks on the left (they go into the selected bar). Click a block to change, move or delete it.
bars.libHelp: A click inserts the block into the selected bar (otherwise at the top).

typeHint.logo: Your company logo. It is fitted to the height of the bar.
typeHint.title: Shows the name of the page currently open.
typeHint.clock: Date and time of the PC.
typeHint.conn: Shows whether easy4Visu is connected to the controllers.
typeHint.text: A fixed text, e.g. the name of the plant.
typeHint.spacer: Pushes the following blocks to the end of the bar.
typeHint.pagekeys: One key per operating page (F1, F2 … in order). The open page is highlighted.
typeHint.fkey: A key with a function of your choice.
typeHint.alarms: Shows the newest open alarm with count and an “Acknowledge” button. Without alarms it shows “no alarms”.
typeHint.login: Shows who is logged in, with a button to log in and out.
typeHint.lang: Key that switches to the next language of the project.

bars.label: Label
bars.labelHint: Empty = matching text for the function.
bars.writeHint: Writes this value when pressed (e.g. 1 = set marker). The easyE4 program resets it itself.
bars.showOnPageHint: Off: this page shows no bars (e.g. for a full-screen diagram).
bars.logoDarkHint: Optional: shown in the dark design instead of the normal logo, e.g. a version with light text.
bars.empty: empty – choose a block on the left
bars.exitNoLogin: Only technicians see the keys “Leave” and “Close easy4Visu”. So that they can log in, put “Login” into a bar (otherwise only via keyboard with Esc).

trend.nowHint: Back to the current time – the curve follows
trend.emptyEditor: Drag variables here – up to 4 curves
trend.noData: Nothing was recorded in this period.

alarms.title: Alarms
alarms.intro: Here you decide which bits trigger an alarm. Faults must be acknowledged, warnings and messages disappear by themselves. easy4Visu only detects alarms while it is connected.
alarms.emptyHint: With “Add alarm” or in the variable list via “As alarm”.
alarms.ackHint: Per device the marker your program uses to reset stored faults (e.g. V_Quittieren). On acknowledging it gets a short pulse: 1, back to 0 after 1 s.
alarms.asAlarmHint: Creates a fault for this bit with the display name as text (can be changed under “Alarms”).
alarms.asAlarmExists: There is already an alarm for this variable.
alarms.ackMissing: Without an acknowledge marker the program does not reset the faults – they only disappear from the list: __list__

auth.locked: Too many failed attempts – login locked, __s__ s left.
auth.needSetup: Please log in as technician for this.
auth.reasonExit: Log in as technician to leave operating mode.
auth.reasonSetup: Log in as technician to set up.
auth.reasonQuit: Log in as technician to close easy4Visu.
auth.usersIntro: Who may do what? Observers only watch, operators switch, set setpoints and acknowledge, technicians may do everything.
auth.firstTitle: No users yet – everything is open
auth.firstHint: First create a technician. From then on login is required, and you are logged in as this technician right away.
auth.secondSetup: Recommendation: create a second technician (e.g. as a deputy). If the only technician password is forgotten, only the emergency access helps.
auth.name: Name
auth.secretHint: At least one of the two. A PIN is quicker on a touch panel.
auth.auditIntro: Who wrote, acknowledged or changed the login when. Nobody can change or delete entries; they are removed after the retention period (set under “Recordings”).
auth.more: The newest __n__ entries are shown; the CSV file contains all.
auth.emergencyHint: easy4Visu was started as Windows administrator with “--notfall”. You can reset a technician password here.
auth.lockedMin: Too many failed attempts – login locked, __m__:__s__ min left.
auth.reasonQuitApp: Log in as technician to close easy4Visu.
auth.quitConfirm: Really close easy4Visu? With “Start with Windows” it only starts again after the next restart of the PC.
auth.reasonStart: Log in to set up. Without logging in you can use the operating pages as __role__.

langs.title: Languages
langs.intro: All texts of your project in all languages. In the editor you write in the base language; here or in Excel you add the translations. If one is missing, the visualisation shows the text of the base language.
langs.baseConfirm: “__name__” as base language? From then on you write in __name__ in the editor – what you type in the editor goes into this column. To only look at it, please use “Test display in”.
langs.empty: No texts yet. They are created by themselves as soon as you add pages, labels or alarms in the editor.
langs.importPh: __id__ “__text__” – placeholders differ from the base language (__lang__)
langs.programHint: Program texts (e.g. “Acknowledge”) exist in German and English; in other languages they appear in English.
langs.langElement: Shows one button for each language of the project.
langs.baseHint: The base language is the language you write in in the editor. Everything you type in the editor goes into this column. To look at another language, do not change the base language – use “Test display in” instead.
langs.viewHint: Switches operating pages and program to this language (like the language selection in operation).
langs.copies: Remove copies of the base language
langs.copiesHint: Clears translations that are exactly the same as the base language text – e.g. after an import that included untranslated rows. They then show as “missing” again.
langs.copiesConfirm: Clear all translations that are exactly the same as the base language text?
langs.editorLangHint: In the editor you write in the base language. Change it under “Languages”.

first.title: First steps
first.varsHint: take over from your easySoft project
first.pageHint: Drag variables onto the page in the editor
first.usersHint: Login, so only technicians can change things

web.loginIntro: Log in with your easy4Visu user.
web.lost: Connection to the visualisation lost – reconnecting … Operation is locked.
web.noPages: No operating pages yet – they are created on the PC in the editor.
web.off: The visualisation is currently not shared on the network.

optWeb.title: Phone and tablet (in the browser)
optWeb.intro: Open the operating pages in the browser on a phone, tablet or another PC on the same network.
optWeb.notAvailable: This feature is not available here.
optWeb.enableHint: Operating pages on a phone, tablet or another PC in the browser – only after logging in. Editor and administration are only available here on the PC.
optWeb.noSetup: Only possible once a setup user has been created under “Users”.
optWeb.portHint: Default 8080. Only change it if another program already uses this port.
optWeb.startPageHint: The browser tells phone and tablet apart by screen size. A browser on a PC counts as a tablet.
optWeb.notInWeb: not in the browser (tick “Show in browser” in the editor)
optWeb.noAddress: No network found – is the PC connected to LAN or Wi-Fi?
optWeb.warn: Unencrypted (HTTP) – only use in the local network (LAN/Wi-Fi), do not expose to the internet.
optWeb.firewall: If Windows asks about the firewall when switching on for the first time: choose “Allow” for private networks.
optWeb.sleep: The PC must be switched on and must not go to sleep.

backup.title: Project
backup.intro: Saves devices, variables, pages, bars, images, alarm texts, text table and design to one file – e.g. for another PC or before bigger changes. Trends, alarm history and audit log are not included.
backup.saveUsersHint: With names, roles and passwords (only as check values, not readable).
backup.saveSecretsHint: Only with a password for the file. Without it, device passwords must be entered again after restoring.
backup.passwordShort: The password must have at least 4 characters.
backup.secretsIn: Contains device passwords. Enter the password to take them over – or leave it empty and enter them again afterwards.
backup.pcSecrets: Device passwords of this PC are included (not readable on other PCs).
backup.noSecrets: Without device passwords: the same devices keep their stored ones.
backup.takeUsersHint: Replaces the current users. Afterwards log in with a user from the backup.
backup.warn: Replaces devices, variables, pages, bars, alarm texts, texts and design. The current state is saved to “Sicherungen” first. The connection is closed and easy4Visu restarts afterwards.
backup.autoHint: Once a day, the last 7 are kept (folder “Sicherungen” in the data folder). With users and this PC’s device passwords.
backup.newIntro: Starts with an empty project – like the first start. The current state is backed up automatically first (see “Existing backups” below) and can be restored at any time.
backup.newUsersHint: Unchecked: like a fresh installation – no login until you create users again; until then anyone at the PC can change everything. The previous users are in the backup.
backup.newKeepHint: Colours, theme and bar template (e.g. your company style) stay. Unchecked: default design.
backup.newWarn: Devices, variables, pages, images, alarm texts and texts are deleted. Program settings stay. Trends, alarm history and operator log are moved to the “Backups” folder. The connection is closed and easy4Visu restarts afterwards.
backup.newDone: New project created. easy4Visu is restarting …

mySymbols.addFolderHint: Add a whole folder – subfolders become groups
mySymbols.empty: No symbols yet. Add your own images with “Files …” or “Folder …”; they are copied into the project. Subfolders become groups.
mySymbols.help: Drag onto the page or click = image element. Right-click: rename, remove.
mySymbols.removeConfirm: Remove “__name__” from “My symbols”? Pages that use the image keep it.
mySymbols.name: Name

records.title: Recordings
records.intro: Save trends and alarms as a table (CSV, opens in Excel) and set how long they are kept.
records.noVars: No variable is being recorded yet. Tick “record” under “Variables” – it is also ticked automatically when you drag a variable into a trend.
records.stepHint: One row per change or per interval step. In the interval, the current value at that moment is used.
records.info: approx. __rows__ rows · __cols__ columns · values in their unit
records.tooMany: That would be __rows__ rows – too many for Excel. Please choose a shorter period or a coarser interval.
records.alarmTitle: Save alarm history as a table
records.alarmCols: Columns: alarm, type, device, came, went, acknowledged
records.keepIntro: easy4Visu deletes older entries by itself.
records.shorter: This deletes all entries older than “__days__”. Continue?
records.keepOnlySetup: Only a setup user can change this.
records.info1: approx. __rows__ rows · 1 column · values in their unit

demo.musterHint: A finished sample project with three simulated easyE4 (compressed air, production, building) – no device and no network needed. Your own project stays untouched.
demo.confirmMuster: easy4Visu now restarts with the Talwerk demo and simulated devices. Your own project stays untouched; changes in the demo are not saved. Continue?
demo.hintOnMuster: easy4Visu shows the Talwerk demo with simulated devices. Changes are not saved. “Stop demo mode” returns to your project.
demo.musterMissing: The Talwerk demo is missing from this installation.
demo.title: Demo mode
demo.band: DEMO – values are simulated, no real plant connected. Changes are not saved.
demo.hint: Restarts easy4Visu with built-in simulators instead of the real easyE4 – for presentations, trade fairs and trying it out. Your project is copied for this; trends, alarms and the operation log of the demo only go into the copy. The next normal start is as before.
demo.hintOn: easy4Visu runs with simulated devices and a copy of your project. Changes in the demo are not saved.
demo.confirmOn: easy4Visu now restarts – with simulated devices and a copy of your project. The real devices are not polled meanwhile. Continue?
demo.confirmOff: easy4Visu now restarts with your real project and the real devices. Changes made in the demo are lost. Continue?
